research_question: Why do public digital received texts assign twelve versus twenty extra fractional parts after twelve lunar limits per day, when the 820-per-limit conversion is otherwise near parallel?

received_witnesses.limitations: Three electronic presentations are not automatically independent transcribed physical originals. The number 12 is not yet visually bound to an institutional Five Li source-native target crop.

received_witnesses.work: Prior Tianwen 13KQ original-image controls, separately source scoped to other Ming/Qing astronomical texts

conditional_arithmetic.premises: One nominal day = 10000 source-base parts, one limit = 820 such parts, with fractional tail read as hundredths of a limit FOR THE SAKE OF TEST ONLY; does not prove historical suffix radix
conditional_arithmetic.twelve_hundredths_approximate_day_parts: 12.12 * 820 = 9938.4 (falls short of nominal day by 61.6 base parts)
conditional_arithmetic.scope: The 20 suffix yields a closer daily approximation under these hypotheses, but arithmetic consistency cannot amend, invent or adjudicate a specific historical printed glyph.

next_gate: The issue stays focused on authenticated early Xu-An v45 B L132 target and original 疾-specific 捷法 and 少/微 radix/carry. Do not repair Five Li digital 十二 to 二十 from arithmetic; either reading requires source-native folio; later 820 explanation and G893 target table remain different evidentiary layers.

edges_rejected_or_unproved: Same Mei attribution and parallel 820 wording do not prove authorial copying identity, archetype or physical edition; suspected digital 12/20 discrepancy is not established historical textual corruption.
unresolved_lineage_questions: Which printed 五禮通考 physical edition, if any, actually carries 十二 instead of 二十, and whether the divergence arose during compilation, printing or modern transcription, is undetermined.
